root_cause: PromptBase.on_validate_error() calls self.console.print(error) with no markup argument, so it inherits the Console's global markup setting. InvalidResponse messages contain style markup such as '[prompt.invalid]Please enter Y or N'. On a Console(markup=False) that tag is printed as literal text instead of being rendered.
best_solution: In rich/prompt.py PromptBase.on_validate_error, change self.console.print(error) to self.console.print(error, markup=True). The error messages are library-authored markup strings, so the library has to force markup on regardless of the console default. Console.print's per-call markup kwarg overrides the console-wide setting. One-line change.

our_outcome_summary: v4, v7 and v8 PASS with byte-identical patches, the same as gold (markup=True added, roughly 35s and 13-16 calls). v6 FAILED with an empty patch (235s). The locator subagent found the correct file, line and root cause within 13s. The fixer subagent then issued about 150 identical edit_file calls whose argument JSON was malformed: the model put the key inside the new_string value (new_string='        self.console.print(error, markup=True)`,old_string:'), so old_string was never sent as a parameter. Every call got 'mandatory input parameters are not present: old_string', and the fixer repeated the same broken call until the budget ran out. This was a tool-call serialization loop, not a reasoning error.
generalizable_lesson: (1) The harness must detect repeated identical tool-call failures. After 2-3 identical 'missing parameter' errors from edit_file, switch the agent to a fallback edit path, such as a line-number replace, a sed/python one-liner through run_command, or a whole-file write. Also try to repair malformed args where a key name leaks into the previous string value (for example '`,old_string:'). If the locator has already given an exact file:line fix, applying a one-line change should not depend on the model producing perfect JSON. (2) Domain pattern: when library-generated output such as error or validation messages is rendered through a user-supplied context (console, logger, formatter), pass the rendering options the message needs explicitly at the call site (markup=True, escape, and so on) rather than inheriting the user's global setting.
acceptable_alternatives: Any change that renders the error message with markup whatever the console setting would pass, for example printing Text.from_markup(error.message) or making InvalidResponse.__rich__ return Text.from_markup(self.message). Stripping the markup tags would also pass this test, since the StringIO output has no ANSI codes, but it drops the intended red style on real terminals. Escaping the tags would fail, because the literal '[prompt.invalid]' text would still be printed.
